task_1.title: Restore HTTPResponse header accessors
task_1.description: The 2.6.1 update restores the previously removed HTTPResponse.getheaders() and HTTPResponse.getheader(name, default) methods so applications and dependent libraries relying on the legacy header accessor API can upgrade without breaking, while continuing to support the newer headers attribute access pattern.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that HTTPResponse remains backward compatible with callers that use the legacy getheaders() and getheader(name, default) methods for response header access after upgrading from 2.6.0 to 2.6.1.

expectation.grounded: BaseHTTPResponse and HTTPResponse must expose getheaders() returning the response headers object and getheader(name, default=None) returning the value from the response headers for the requested name, or the supplied default when no value is present. These methods must coexist with HTTPResponse.headers and preserve the existing HTTPHeaderDict-based lookup behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to access response headers through either the legacy method-based API or the headers attribute, with equivalent observable results and without compatibility breakage for dependent libraries.

constraints.grounded: Restoring getheaders() and getheader(name, default) must not remove, replace, or change HTTPResponse.headers, HTTPResponse.info(), or existing HTTPHeaderDict lookup semantics. The default value behavior of getheader must match the headers collection's get behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The compatibility fix should add back the removed public methods without changing existing header access behavior or weakening support for the newer attribute-based API.

behavior: HTTPResponse instances provide a getheaders() method again.
Calling getheaders() returns the same response header collection exposed through the headers attribute.
HTTPResponse instances provide a getheader(name, default=None) method again.
Calling getheader with an existing header name returns the corresponding header value using the response headers collection's normal lookup semantics.
Calling getheader with a missing header name returns None by default or the caller-provided default value when one is supplied.
The restored methods are available through the shared base response behavior used by HTTPResponse.
acceptance_criteria: Given an HTTPResponse with headers, when getheaders() is called, then it should return the response's headers collection.
Given an HTTPResponse with a matching header, when getheader(name) is called, then it should return the same value available from the headers collection for that name.
Given an HTTPResponse without a matching header, when getheader(name) is called without a default, then it should return None.
Given an HTTPResponse without a matching header, when getheader(name, default) is called with a default value, then it should return that default value.
When callers use HTTPResponse.headers or HTTPResponse.info(), their existing behavior should remain unchanged.
